description:
Make `jit init` decide whether to claim the `.gitattributes` merge driver from the layout the invocation already detected, instead of starting `git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree` again.

## Background

- `gitattributes_claim` (`crates/jit/src/commands/init.rs:524-535`), called once per initialization (`crates/jit/src/commands/init.rs:175`), calls `worktree_is_git_work_tree` (`crates/jit/src/commands/init.rs:539-548`), which starts git a second time per `jit init`.
- The executor holds the invocation's `WorktreePaths` (`require_worktree_paths`, `crates/jit/src/commands/mod.rs:2240`), which already say whether the worktree is a git checkout.
- CLI tests assert the merge-driver line in a git repository (`crates/jit/tests/cli_repo_workflow/init_tests.rs:519`).
- Kept as one change for a build reason: `worktree_is_git_work_tree` is private, and an uncalled private function fails the zero-warning build.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The merge-driver claim is eligible exactly when the executor's paths are a git checkout and the data root lies beneath the worktree root. `worktree_is_git_work_tree` no longer exists and `commands/init.rs` starts no process.
- [hard] REQ-02: A unit test initializes a real git work tree through an executor whose paths classify it as outside git and asserts no merge-driver claim; today's code claims one because it asks git directly.
- [hard] REQ-03: The init CLI tests pass unchanged.

## Notes

- Written against the code as it stands after the changes this one follows; line citations name current code.
title: Init reads git classification from the invocation's layout
